subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should global or per-agent exec security config always override previously persisted per-session `/exec` host/security/ask/node fields after config changes, and what migration or reset path should existing session entries get?
rationale: Current source and docs make `/exec` durable session state, but the reported behavior can preserve a weaker session exec policy after an operator tightens config; automation cannot choose that security/product boundary safely.

options.title: Operator policy wins with reset/migration
options.body: Make global or per-agent exec security floors dominate stale stored session exec fields after config changes and add doctor, reset, or migration coverage for existing entries.

options.title: Keep durable `/exec` session defaults
options.body: Treat current behavior as intentional and document that operators must hard-disable exec through tool policy or explicitly clear affected sessions.

options.title: Add explicit operator reset only
options.body: Keep current precedence but add an operator-facing command or doctor fix to clear stored exec directives per channel, session, or agent.

recommendation.title: Operator policy wins with reset/migration
recommendation.body: Make global or per-agent exec security floors dominate stale stored session exec fields after config changes and add doctor, reset, or migration coverage for existing entries.

likelyOwner.reason: The original `/exec` session override behavior and current docs/tests trace most directly to this history.
